title: When, before and after
explanation: Όταν introduces “when”, while πριν can introduce a clause for an action occurring later than the main action. Μετά can precede a noun phrase, as in μετά το μάθημα; distinguish a clause containing a verb from a prepositional phrase containing a noun.
formation: όταν + clause; πριν + nonpast clause; μετά + accusative noun phrase

examples.translation: When I have time, I read.
I close the door before I leave.

examples.text: Θα πάμε για καφέ μετά το μάθημα.
examples.translation: We will go for coffee after the lesson.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: ___ έχω χρόνο, διαβάζω.
When I have time, I read.
exercises.explanation: Όταν έχω χρόνο, διαβάζω. — When I have time, I read. Όταν introduces “when”, while πριν can introduce a clause for an action occurring later than the main action. Μετά can precede a noun phrase, as in μετά το μάθημα; distinguish a clause containing a verb from a prepositional phrase containing a noun.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Κλείνω την πόρτα πριν ___.
I close the door before I leave.
exercises.explanation: Κλείνω την πόρτα πριν φύγω. — I close the door before I leave. Όταν introduces “when”, while πριν can introduce a clause for an action occurring later than the main action. Μετά can precede a noun phrase, as in μετά το μάθημα; distinguish a clause containing a verb from a prepositional phrase containing a noun.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Θα πάμε για καφέ μετά ___ μάθημα.
We will go for coffee after the lesson.
exercises.explanation: Θα πάμε για καφέ μετά το μάθημα. — We will go for coffee after the lesson. Όταν introduces “when”, while πριν can introduce a clause for an action occurring later than the main action. Μετά can precede a noun phrase, as in μετά το μάθημα; distinguish a clause containing a verb from a prepositional phrase containing a noun.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means “after work”?
exercises.explanation: Μετά takes an accusative noun phrase here: τη δουλειά.

exercises.prompt: Choose “before I leave”.
exercises.explanation: The intended future-relative action uses πριν with φύγω, not a past indicative form.

explanation: The present perfect uses a form of έχω plus an invariable perfective form, such as έχω γράψει or έχω δει. It often connects a past experience or result to the present; only έχω changes for person and number, and a specific finished past time commonly favors the aorist.

title: Duration continuing until now: εδώ και
explanation: Εδώ και followed by a duration can describe a situation that began earlier and continues now. Greek commonly uses the present in this construction, where English may use “have been”; do not confuse it with πριν από, which locates an event a duration ago.

title: Always, often and every day
explanation: Πάντα, συχνά and μερικές φορές describe frequency, while κάθε with a singular noun means “every”. Frequency expressions can move for emphasis, but κάθε itself is invariable and does not take a plural ending.

title: Clock time: στη μία and στις δύο
explanation: To state the time, use είναι μία for one o’clock and είναι δύο, τρεις and so on for other hours. To say when an event occurs, use στη μία but στις δύο; half past follows the gender of the understood ώρα, giving μία και μισή.

title: Weekdays and dates

title: Nobody, nothing and nowhere

title: Someone, something and somewhere

exercises.explanation: Είδα κάποιον στον κήπο. — I saw someone in the garden. Κάποιος/κάποια/κάποιο refer to an unspecified person or thing and change for gender, number and case. Κάτι means “something” and κάπου means “somewhere”; neither inflects like κάποιος, so choose the form for the intended role.

exercises.prompt: Choose “The keys are somewhere here”.
exercises.explanation: Κάπου is the invariable adverb referring to an unspecified place.

exercises.prompt: Complete the subject: ___ γυναίκα σε περιμένει.
exercises.explanation: The indefinite word agrees with feminine singular γυναίκα: κάποια.
